meaningful_changes: External module refreshed to October 5 with 17 of 22 fresh context series; China futures, physical and options remained on the September 30 last-good snapshot.
Brent fell from 103.06 to 102.44 and WTI from 91.57 to 90.31 between the morning anchor and 19:07 BJT, so the Saudi attack premium did not extend.
ICE gasoil rose more than 4 percent to 1409 dollars per tonne while crude was flat-to-lower, isolating a refined-product and logistics squeeze rather than a broad crude breakout.
LME copper and SGX iron ore were only about 0.5 percent above October 2 repo anchors; COMEX silver rose about 2.6 percent and ICE sugar about 4.8 percent, but China confirmation is unavailable.

The former long FU versus short SC expression remains cancelled because diesel tightness is not an exact proxy for high-sulphur fuel oil and external evidence supports SC tail risk more than the old hedge.
